callees.name: _parse_spec_conditions
callees.pre_condition: spec is a dict that contains the keys 'pre_condition' and 'post_condition', each mapping to a string.
callees.post_condition: Returns a pair (pre, post) where pre is the string value associated with the 'pre_condition' key in spec and post is the string value associated with the 'post_condition' key in spec.

callees.name: _split_into_blocks_braced
callees.pre_condition: func is a non-empty string containing the source code of a single function. language is a non-empty string identifying the programming language of func.
callees.post_condition: Returns an ordered list of block strings, each a contiguous segment of func. The concatenation of all blocks in order reconstructs the original function body. Each split point occurs at a line where brace depth returns to the entry depth for the language, so that no block begins or ends inside an incomplete compound statement.

callees.name: _generate_block_post_condition
callees.signature: _generate_block_post_condition(block: str, current_pre: str, info: str, language: str, trace_dir: str | None = None, trace_meta: dict | None = None) -> str
callees.pre_condition: block is a non-empty string containing the source code of one code block. current_pre is a string describing the pre-condition that holds when control enters the block. info is a string of contextual knowledge (may be empty). language is a non-empty string identifying the programming language. trace_dir, when provided, is a writable directory path; trace_meta is a dict of trace metadata.
callees.post_condition: Returns a string describing the post-condition that the block guarantees after execution, given that current_pre held when control entered the block. Returns an empty string if the post-condition could not be generated.

callees.name: _has_terminating_statement
callees.pre_condition: block is a string containing source code. language is a non-empty string identifying the programming language.
callees.post_condition: Returns True when the block contains at least one statement that unconditionally terminates or transfers control flow (such as a return, break, continue, raise, exit, or the language-equivalent) in the given language, so that statements after the block would not execute along that path. Returns False when no such terminating statement is present in the block.

callees.name: _check_post_implies_spec
callees.signature: _check_post_implies_spec(block: str, post_condition: str, spec_post_condition: str, info: str, language: str, trace_dir: str | None = None, trace_meta: dict | None = None) -> tuple[bool, str, str, str]
callees.pre_condition: block is a string containing the source code of one code block. post_condition is a non-empty string describing the computed post-condition that block guarantees after execution. spec_post_condition is a non-empty string describing the post-condition required by the function's specification. info is a string of contextual knowledge (may be empty). language is a non-empty string identifying the programming language. trace_dir, when provided, is a writable directory path; trace_meta is a dict of trace metadata.
callees.post_condition: Returns a 4-tuple (passed, offending_statements, conflicting_post_condition, reason). When the computed post_condition logically implies the spec_post_condition, passed is True and the remaining elements are empty strings. When the implication does not hold, passed is False: offending_statements describes the code from the block whose behaviour violates the spec, conflicting_post_condition restates the post_condition whose guarantee is broken, and reason explains the condition under which the violation occurs.
